intended_object: The `RatFunc S`-algebra structure on the constant-field extension `ExactConstantExtension C N S` (roughly N ⊗_C S). It is obtained from the canonical embedding of S(X) into that extension, which exists when C is algebraically closed in N. The docstring and its uses as a `let`/instance in later files show this.
explanation: This is a technical device, not a mathematical object in its own right. The body is just `RingHom.toAlgebra` applied to the previously defined ring hom `ratFuncToExactConstantExtension`. It is marked `@[reducible]` and exists so that later files (ConstantExtensionInfinityPlaceBridge, ExactConstantExtensionNormalClosureTower and others) can install the `Algebra (RatFunc S) _` instance locally with `let`. All the mathematical content is in the underlying ring hom. Packaging that hom as an algebra structure is an implementation detail of how Lean handles instances, so it has no separate counterpart in the literature to compare against.
